title: Understand any sentence
summary: Find the engine that ends the sentence, work out where each clause stops, and treat everything else as a modifier. A hidden main carriage is a zero.

blocks.text: Every logical clause has a **main carriage** (the one the clause is about) and an **engine** (the verb, adjective, or noun + だ that says what is true of it). The engine is usually visible. The main carriage is often a **zero**, hidden but always there. The difficulty with long sentences is finding where each clause begins and ends.
Clues for where a clause ends

items: The **head clause** ends the sentence at its last engine: a verb, an adjective, or だ / です after a noun.
Particles like よ and ね come after the sentence is over; they are not part of the clause.
A noun followed by **な** is a modifier, not a clause engine: きれいな花.
A clause that is not last ends in an engine plus a connector: a **て-form**, an **い-stem**, or a **conditional**.

blocks.text: 傘を持って来ればよかった. The first clause ends in 持って来れば (a conditional is a connector), so another clause must follow. The last clause is よかった: an engine that ends the sentence. Its main carriage is a zero: "it", the situation in general. Compare 晴れだね: nobody says what "is sunny", yet the sentence works.
A verb without its own connector that comes before a noun simply describes that noun.

blocks.jp: 日本語が話せる留学生は、金メダルを取った女性と結婚した。
blocks.en: The exchange student who can speak Japanese married a woman who won a gold medal.

blocks.text: Work from the end: the head engine is 結婚した. 日本語が話せる describes 留学生, and 金メダルを取った describes 女性. So there is one clause, with the main carriage 留学生は and two modifiers.

items: Look for the last engine first.
Connectors (て, い-stem, ば, たら) mean "another clause follows".
A verb with no connector before a noun is a modifier.

questions.instruction: Tap the engine of the head clause
questions.note: The head clause ends the sentence at its engine.
questions.en: My older brother goes to school by bicycle every day.

questions.instruction: Tap the engine of the head clause
questions.note: 中止です: noun + です ends the sentence.
questions.en: If it rains, the game is canceled.

questions.instruction: Tap the connector that links the first clause to the next
questions.note: The て-form means another clause follows.
questions.en: I ate breakfast and went out.

questions.instruction: Tap the verb that is only a modifier
questions.note: A verb with no connector before a noun describes it.
questions.en: The book I bought yesterday is interesting.

questions.instruction: How many clauses does this have?
questions.prompt: 本を読んでから、お風呂に入った。
questions.note: 読んで is a connector, so another clause follows.
questions.en: After reading the book, I took a bath.

questions.instruction: What is 友達が作った here?
questions.prompt: 友達が作ったケーキを食べた。
questions.note: A verb with no connector before a noun describes it.
questions.en: I ate the cake my friend made.

questions.instruction: Who is the main carriage?
options: A zero: the thing in general
questions.note: The carriage is hidden but always there.

questions.instruction: Which part sits outside the clause, added after the sentence is over?
questions.note: よ comes after the sentence is over.
questions.en: I can't go tomorrow, you know.

questions.instruction: What does 静かな do here?
questions.prompt: 静かな町に住んでいる。
questions.note: Noun + な points to a following noun.
questions.en: I live in a quiet town.

questions.instruction: Which ending shows that the clause is NOT the last one?
questions.note: A て-form is a connector.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: きれいな in きれいな花 is the engine of its own clause.
questions.note: Noun + な is a modifier, not a clause engine.
questions.en: A pretty flower: きれいな describes the noun.

questions.instruction: Where should you start reading a long sentence?
questions.note: The head clause ends the sentence.

questions.instruction: What is the head engine?
questions.prompt: 赤いかばんを持った女の子が走っている。
questions.note: 持った and 赤い only describe nouns.
questions.en: A girl carrying a red bag is running.

questions.instruction: Who is the main carriage of the head clause?
questions.prompt: 昨日会った友達は、医者になった。
questions.note: 会った only describes 友達.
questions.en: The friend I met yesterday became a doctor.

questions.instruction: In the course's terms the main carriage is the subject. Which sentence has no subject said aloud?
questions.note: Nobody says who bought the book.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: The child who is sleeping is my younger brother.
questions.note: Modifier, carriage, engine.
questions.en: The child who is sleeping is my younger brother.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I ate the cake my mother made.
questions.note: The modifier goes before the noun.
questions.en: I ate the cake my mother made.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I got home and took a bath.
questions.note: て-form, then the last clause.
questions.en: I got home and took a bath.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: If it gets cold, I will wear a coat.
questions.note: A conditional clause, then the head clause.
questions.en: If it gets cold, I will wear a coat.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: The man running in the park is my father.
questions.note: Modifier, carriage, engine.
questions.en: The man running in the park is my father.

questions.instruction: Tap the engine of the head clause
questions.note: おいしかった ends the sentence.
